02 · The solution
The watch notices the attack by itself.
1
Guard Mode on

She switches it on when she feels unsafe. Otherwise, it is a normal smartwatch.

2
A stranger's touch → 15-second PIN

A grab, a pull or a struggle. It vibrates, starts recording and asks for her PIN.

3
No PIN → family + 112 alerted

Her live GPS location and audio go out over its own 4G SIM.

4
Forced to cancel? Duress PIN

The screen says "Cancelled" while the alert is sent silently.

Her own hand: ignored Watch ripped off: instant alert
03 · How it knows
Two signals tell a stranger from her own hand.
Signal 1 · Touch sweep
Is a hand on the strap?
A tiny signal sweeps through the strap. Any hand on it moves the reading by ~16%, against 0.1% noise.
Signal 2 · Static charge
Is it another body?
Every body carries its own static charge. When another person touches her, it evens out and her voltage jumps.

04 · The product
A flagship 4G smartwatch, with a safety core inside.
Own nano-SIM: 4G VoLTE calls and SMS
Built-in GPS, live location
1.43″ AMOLED, always-on, crown
Heart rate · SpO₂ · ECG · skin temperature
Wi-Fi 6 · Bluetooth 5.3 · NFC
500 mAh · wireless charging
Two processors. One runs the apps; a separate safety core runs Guard Mode alone, so a frozen app can never block an alert. Our own SparshaOS, on open-source Zephyr.
